speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific movements you've noticed in your hands, and have you or a family member noticed any changes in your memory or thinking lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed description. Has he experienced any stiffness, slowness of movement, or balance problems besides the tremor? Also, has he noticed any changes in his speech, mood, or sleep patterns?

REQUEST TEST: Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)
REQUEST TEST: DAT_Scan

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease. The combination of unilateral resting tremor, soft speech (hypophonia), reduced facial expressions (masked face), and executive dysfunction (difficulty managing finances) is highly characteristic of Parkinson's disease, making the previous suggestion of iron deficiency anemia unlikely. I will proceed with a DAT scan to confirm the diagnosis.
